source_item.title: Rho-Bank flyer promotions could not be verified; human transfer completed
source_item.body: In a Rho-Bank customer-service interaction, the customer said they had mailed promotional flyers and first asked about a $1,000 statement credit after spending $10,000 in two months. Searches found a similar Business Bronze offer for $500 (and the customer said they were not a business owner), but no confirmation of the customer's $1,000 flyer. The customer then asked about two other flyers: zero foreign transaction fees for three years and a first-year annual fee waiver. Searches found examples of standard 0% foreign transaction fees on some cards, fees on others, and a Platinum card document that mentioned a first-year fee waiver conditionally; none established either flyer-specific promotion or this customer's eligibility. The assistant repeatedly stated it could not confirm or apply the flyer terms and offered human review. After the customer persisted in demanding one of the unavailable offers, the assistant invoked transfer_to_human_agents with reason customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal. The tool returned “Transfer successful” and said a human agent would assist shortly. Afterward, customer again tried to get the $1,000 credit approved and later directly requested a human; assistant said the existing referral was already in place. Observed outcome: a transfer was reported successful. Unknown: whether an agent actually connected, whether any flyer was genuine or eligible, and whether any offer was honored. The searches and conclusions only reflect the information available in that conversation.

source_item.title: Rho-Bank flyer promotions were unverified; human transfer succeeded
source_item.body: Observed conversation: A customer said mailed Rho-Bank flyers advertised (1) a $1,000 statement credit after spending $10,000 in the first two months, (2) $0 foreign transaction fees for three years, and (3) a first-year annual-fee waiver. The customer said they were not a business owner and worked at a power plant. KB searches surfaced a Business Bronze Rewards Card offer for $500 after $10,000 spend in two months, not the customer's claimed $1,000; card information showed differing standard foreign-transaction-fee terms, and a Platinum Rewards Card article mentioned first-year waivers only as a conditional case. None of those results verified the specific flyer offers or the customer's eligibility. The assistant did not apply or promise any offer. After repeated insistence, the assistant invoked transfer_to_human_agents with reason customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal; tool response was “Transfer successful” and said a human agent would assist shortly. The customer subsequently requested transfer again; assistant stated they had already been referred. Inference/limits: This records only what the supplied conversation and KB results showed. It does not establish whether the flyers were genuine, whether the customer qualified, whether the human agent ultimately connected, or whether any offer was honored.

source_item.title: Referral link request: Crypto-Cash Back unresolved, Business Gold succeeded
source_item.body:
In the conversation, the user first asked for a Crypto-Cash Back card referral link based on a mailed offer claiming $100 after a referred person spent $500 in their first two months. The assistant searched the knowledge base and reported it could not confirm either that card's referral program or those terms; it did not provide a link tool and suggested checking in-app/online banking or contacting support. This establishes only that the available knowledge-base results did not confirm the offer, not whether the letter or offer was valid.

The user then asked about the Business Gold Rewards Card, citing $200 for $7,500 spend within 90 days. A first search returned no matches, but a broader search produced a result documenting a $200 bonus, $7,500 qualifying spend within 90 days, up to 8 yearly bonuses, and acceptance of new referrals only until September 15, 2025. The assistant said the cited terms matched and tried to provide the user tool, but the user reported that it had not actually been given. The assistant then explicitly gave the get_referral_link tool; its response said the tool was now available and required no arguments. The user subsequently reported, “That worked! I've got my referral link now.” Thus the observed outcome is the user's report of successful link generation; no link contents or independent tool execution result were shown in the conversation. This experience does not establish whether the offer remains available after the documented cutoff.

source_item.title: Referral link tool provided after initial misdirection
source_item.body:
Observed in the provided conversation: the user first asked about a Crypto-Cash Back card referral offer claiming $100 for a referred person's $500 spend in their first 2 months. Knowledge-base search results did not document that card or those terms; the assistant said it could not confirm them and advised checking the app/online banking or calling 1-800-RHO-BANK.

The user then asked about the Business Gold Rewards Card and described $200 for $7,500 spend within 90 days. Search results included a specific Business Gold Rewards Card referral entry documenting $200, qualifying $7,500 spend within 90 days, a cap of 8 bonuses per calendar year, and acceptance of new referrals only until 2025-09-15. Internal instructions said customer must generate the link themselves and quoted a tool signature requiring user_id and exact card name. However, the assistant subsequently surfaced the discoverable user tool as `get_referral_link` with no arguments; the user said it then worked and they obtained their link. This is evidence of the user reporting success, not an independently observed tool result or proof that the generated link was valid or the referral qualifies.

The assistant initially told the user the tool was provided before actually giving it. After the user reported it was unavailable, the assistant gave it via `give_discoverable_user_tool`, and then the user reported success. This episode does not establish that a no-argument procedure is generally correct; it conflicts with the internal knowledge-base instruction specifying `user_id` and `card_name`. Preserve this discrepancy and do not generalize beyond this conversation.
